source_preflight.notes: Prevalence: no claim is made about how common/rare the marking is; the FAQ explicitly states the two sources don't address frequency rather than asserting either direction. Historical/traditional claims: every interpretive statement is attributed specifically to Cheiro or to Benham, matching the two evidence notes; no claim exceeds what each note's 'safe claim boundary' / 'safe use' section authorizes. Location/identification: Benham's path and Cheiro's Mount-of-Jupiter/Plate-XX placement are each attributed to their source, and the 'How cautiously to identify it' section explicitly flags that only one source gives a specific arc rather than presenting the geometry as universally agreed. Combination readings: the 'in context' section states only that the mount and the ring share interpretive territory in Cheiro/Benham's own writing and explicitly declines to state any further combined reading beyond what each source says on its own; Benham's own 'other chirognomic indications' condition is preserved without inventing which indications those are. Vague attribution: no 'modern palmists'/'some writers'/'experts' phrasing anywhere; myth-section corrections state what the two named sources do and don't say rather than attributing the myths to an unnamed authority. Quotation fidelity: no quotation marks are used around any Cheiro/Benham content — all paraphrased per the evidence notes' 'paraphrased rather than quoted unless independently re-verified verbatim' instruction; the myth-section bolded phrases are reader-voiced hypothetical claims in the site's established myth-format convention (see mount-of-jupiter.md), not source quotations. Claim-type separation: location/associations sections are source-attributed; 'How cautiously to identify it' and the FAQ disclaimers are explicit Palmistry Path editorial/procedural framing, kept visibly distinct. Safety boundaries: no medical, legal, financial, relationship-outcome, or predictive-science claim; all interpretive language uses grounded framing ('Cheiro connected', 'Benham associated', 'within his own system').
